reading.body:
Rashida Tlaib's AI record is almost entirely legislative: 15 of 19 dated events are bills she sponsored or cosponsored, and four are recorded votes.

The bills cluster around two subjects. One is data centers and their physical footprint: a moratorium on AI data centers, a ban on AI data centers on federal lands, site selection transparency, community impact, and environmental impacts. The other is algorithmic harm: civil rights, algorithmic accountability, bias in algorithmic systems, chatbot transparency, and price gouging. Facial recognition and biometric surveillance appear as a separate thread. This is a legislator working the demand side of compute, the buildings and land and power that data centers require, alongside the civil liberties side of automated decisions.

The dates run from March 2025 to September 2026 and are ordered newest first. The record shows sustained activity rather than a single intervention, with at least one AI-related bill or vote in most months covered. The two most recent entries, a facial recognition moratorium cosponsorship and a data center federal lands bill she sponsored herself, sit at the top of the list.

What the data does not show is outcome. Every bill entry carries the latest status date, not a passage or failure, and the four votes are procedural motions to suspend the rules. Nothing here establishes that any bill became law, that any vote decided a policy, or that these positions changed anything about where data centers get built or powered. The summary also mentions money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, but no such event appears in the 19 points, so the financial side of this record is claimed and not shown.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Rashida Tlaib: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 19 events.
